original_question: The gene that causes Myhre syndrome belongs to which family of proteins that modulate members of the TGFβ protein superfamily?

final_qi.question: The gene that causes Myhre syndrome belongs to which family of proteins that modulate members of the TGFβ protein superfamily?
final_qi.long_answer: Myhre syndrome is caused by heterozygous gain-of-function mutations in the SMAD4 gene. SMAD4 encodes a member of the SMAD family, a group of intracellular signalling proteins that bind and modulate signals from ligands of the transforming growth factor-β (TGFβ) superfamily. Thus, the disease-causing gene belongs to the SMAD family of TGFβ signal modulators.
